 Jaguar to recall about 94,000 US vehicles over rearview camera issue, NHTSA says
 Updated - Oct. 23, 2026 at 9:46 a.m.
 | Posted - Oct. 23, 2026 at 2:03 a.m. 
 R Reuters Reuters   
 FILE PHOTO: The Jaguar logo is seen at the Jaguar Land Rover booth during a media day for the Auto Shanghai show in Shanghai, China April 19, 2021. (REUTERS/Aly Song/ File Photo)

 Estimated read time: Less than a minute
 Oct 23 — Jaguar Land Rover ​will recall 93,997 vehicles in the United ‌States as the rearview camera image ⁠may ​fail to ⁠appear on the display, ‌the US National ‌Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) ⁠said ⁠on Friday.
 Here are some more details:
 • NHTSA said insufficient drain holes may trap water in the ‌rearview camera ​and damage it.
 • The recall affects certain 2022-2026 Land Rover Range Rover vehicles, according to the auto safety regulator.
 • ​Dealers will drill ‌additional ‌drain holes ⁠in the underside of the tailgate trim and replace the camera ‌if needed, NHTSA ​said.
 (Reporting by ‌Sumedha ⁠Mukherjee ​in Bengaluru; Editing by Shounak ​Dasgupta)
